title: Trust and Safety Note — Property-Damage Look-Back by Party Record (Listings Extra-Guest Fees)
content:
# Property-Damage Look-Back by Party Record

*Trust and Safety note for Roamhaven Listings, read against the host's Host Accounts record.*

## Rule

When a listing's extra-guest ceiling is worked out on the day of an extra-guest fee reset, the verified losses of its approved property-damage claims are read over a damage look-back. The standard damage look-back is the last **12** whole months before the day of the reset, a claim falling within it according to the date part of its filing moment.

Because the party ban applies to every space type and large extra-guest parties are where party damage arises, the damage look-back follows the party record of the host account the listing belongs to, as its Host Accounts record shows it:

- when a strike of type **party violation** was recorded on the host account within the last twelve months (fewer than twelve whole months before the day of the reset), the damage look-back is lengthened to the last **36** whole months;
- when no such strike was recorded in the last twelve months but one was recorded at least twelve and fewer than twenty-four whole months back, it is the last **24** whole months;
- otherwise the standard damage look-back of the last 12 whole months applies.

## Decision table

| Most recent party-violation strike on the host account | Property-damage losses are read over |
|---|---|
| fewer than 12 whole months back | the last 36 whole months |
| at least 12 and fewer than 24 whole months back | the last 24 whole months |
| 24 whole months back or more, or none | the last 12 whole months |

## Cases (hypothetical host accounts)

- A party-violation strike recorded eight months ago, and another thirty months ago: the first is within twelve months, so 36 whole months.
- A single party-violation strike recorded eighteen months ago: 24 whole months.
- A misrepresentation strike recorded three months ago and no party-violation strike: 12 whole months.
